deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 61-63): Grothendieck is preparing his Nov.-Dec. 1967 talk on crystals. He computes the cohomology of the infinitesimal and crystalline sites by a Čech-type complex.

On the previous page the case where X is formally smooth over S was done. There the formal object X~ is the final object (or covers it). Section 6 now treats the case where X is not formally smooth (for instance in characteristic p).

This page assumes an S-immersion X ↪ Y with Y formally smooth over S. It lists when such an embedding exists:
- locally on X;
- globally if S and X are affine;
- if X is quasi-projective over S, admitting an ample sheaf (bracketed remark).

Let Y(i) be the i-th infinitesimal neighbourhood of X in Y. Each Y(i) is a thickening of X, hence an object of the site. The ind-object Y~ = lim_i Y(i) is the formal completion of Y along X, viewed as a sheaf on the site.

Key step: formal smoothness of Y over S implies that Y~ covers the final object of the topos. Every thickening (U, T) admits, locally, an S-map T → Y extending U ⊂ X ⊂ Y. Since T is a nilpotent thickening, this map factors through some Y(i).

Hence the Čech nerve ν ↦ Y~^{ν+1} (products taken in the topos) gives a Čech/descent spectral sequence:
H^*(X_cris, F) ⇐ E_2^{pq} = H^p(ν ↦ H^q(Y~^{ν+1}, F)).
Here Y~^{ν+1} is the formal completion of Y^{ν+1} (product over S) along the diagonal copy of X.

On the next page: for X affine, Y affine and F quasi-coherent, E_2^{pq} = 0 for q ≠ 0. This gives H^*(X_cris, F) = H^*(ν ↦ F(Y^{ν+1}/X)), the Čech–Alexander complex. The non-affine case is then sheafified on X_zar as a cosimplicial sheaf, leading to hypercohomology.

Purpose: show that crystalline/infinitesimal cohomology can be computed from any smooth embedding. This is the route to the de Rham comparison (Poincaré lemma).
errors: The page is labelled 'cris' (crystalline, characteristic p) but uses the ordinary infinitesimal neighbourhoods Y(i) and the formal completion. For the genuine crystalline site with divided powers one must use the divided-power (PD) envelope of X in Y (or of the diagonal in Y^{ν+1}), not the formal completion. As written, the argument computes infinitesimal cohomology; this distinction is exactly what Berthelot later made precise. Possibly Grothendieck intends PD neighbourhoods implicitly, or this sketch predates that correction.
Minor gap: the claim that Y~ covers the final object needs the lifting to be local on the thickening T. That is fine, but it is not stated.

ideas.what: Computing cohomology of the infinitesimal/crystalline topos via an embedding into a formally smooth Y, using the formal completion as a covering of the final object and the Čech nerve of its powers.
ideas.modern_name: Čech–Alexander complex / Čech–Alexander spectral sequence for crystalline cohomology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes, 1966/68); Berthelot (thesis, SLN 407, 1974) in the PD setting; Berthelot–Ogus, Notes on crystalline cohomology §5
ideas.where_published: Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (notes by Coates–Jussila), sections on the infinitesimal site

ideas.what: Existence conditions for smooth embeddings: locally, for affine S and X, or for X quasi-projective with an ample sheaf.
ideas.modern_name: embeddable schemes / global smooth embedding hypothesis
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Grothendieck, Hartshorne's algebraic de Rham cohomology)
ideas.where_published: Crystals and de Rham cohomology (Dix exposés)

ideas.what: Formal smoothness of Y implies that the ind-object lim Y(i) is an epimorphism onto the final object of the topos.
ideas.modern_name: covering of the final object / weakly final object of the crystalline site

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard sketch of the Čech–Alexander computation of infinitesimal/crystalline cohomology, which appears in Grothendieck's 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' and in Berthelot's work. The only notable feature is the use of ordinary rather than divided-power neighbourhoods under the label 'cris', which is a gap rather than a new idea.
transcription_corrections: 'loct[?] sur X' is struck through; the list of embedding types reads roughly: '[types possibles: localement sur X, ou si S, X affines, ou si X est quasi-projectif sur S admettant un faisceau ample]'. The struck word near 'S' before 'admettant' should be ignored.
'constellations' is doubtful; the sense is 'considérons la famille des objets (épaississements) du site cristallin de X/S représentés par (X,Y)'.
In the displayed limit, Y~ = lim_i Y(i) with tilde over Y(i) (the sheaves represented by Y(i)); the arrow is a direct limit (lim with right arrow).
'l'hypothèse que Y est fᵗ lisse sur S implique que Y~ couvre le faisceau final', i.e. 'est un recouvrement de l'objet final'; 'comme le faisceau' is likely a misreading.
The spectral sequence should read H^*(X_cris, F) ⇐ E_2^{pq} = H^p(ν ↦ H^q(Y~^{ν+1}, F)).
